subject: math
title: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems within 100
seo_title: Grade 2 Word Problems within 100 Worksheets: Add To, Take From, Compare, Bar Models and Two-Step Problems
standard_text: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 word problem worksheets within 100: add to, take from, put together, take apart and compare stories, missing start or change with bar models and ☐ equations, and two-step problems. 100 practice questions with simple answers.
key_big: Picture the story. Then decide: add or subtract?
key_sub: Find what you do not know: the start, the change or the end. Draw a bar model and write an equation with a ☐. The word “more” does not always mean add.
body_html:
Picture the story first

Do not hunt for key words. Ask: what is happening? Is something added, taken away, put together or compared? Then find what you do not know. It can be the start, the change or the end.

Five kinds of stories

KindStoryEquation
Add toMia had 24 stickers. She got 17 more. How many now?24 + 17 = ☐
Take from32 birds were in a tree. 15 flew away. How many are left?32 − 15 = ☐
Put togetherLeo has 26 red and 18 blue marbles. How many in all?26 + 18 = ☐
Take apart52 marbles. 27 are red. The rest are blue. How many are blue?27 + ☐ = 52
CompareSam has 40 cards. Ava has 28. How many more does Sam have?28 + ☐ = 40

Draw a bar model

A bar model shows the parts and the whole. If you know the whole, subtract to find a part. If you know both parts, add.

For a compare story, draw two bars. The extra part is the difference.

Use a box for the unknown

Write an equation and put a ☐ where the unknown number goes. The box can be anywhere.

Example

Some birds were in a tree. 8 flew away. Now 15 are left. How many birds were there at first?

We do not know the start: ☐ − 8 = 15. Put the 8 back: 15 + 8 = 23.

Answer: 23 birds

Example

Sam has 12 more cards than Ava. Sam has 40 cards. How many cards does Ava have?

Sam has more, so Ava has fewer: 40 − 12 = 28. The word “more” does not always mean add.

Answer: 28 cards

Two-step problems

Some stories need two steps. Find the first answer, then use it.

Example

Ava has 25 shells. Leo has 8 more shells than Ava. How many shells do they have in all?

Step 1: Leo has 25 + 8 = 33 shells. Step 2: in all, 25 + 33 = 58. Equation: 25 + 25 + 8 = ☐.

Answer: 58 shells

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding because the story says “more”Ask who has more. If you know the bigger number, subtract.
Adding both numbers when the whole is givenIf you know the whole, subtract to find the part
Forgetting to regroup (37 + 25 = 52)7 + 5 = 12 ones. That is 1 ten and 2 ones: 62
Taking the small digit from the big one (52 − 27 = 35)Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 7 = 5, 4 − 2 = 2. So 25.
Stopping after step 1Read the question again. What does it ask?

faq.q: What kinds of word problems do 2nd graders solve?
faq.a: They solve adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart and compare problems with numbers up to 100. The unknown can be the start, the change or the result, and some problems take two steps.

faq.q: What is a bar model (tape diagram) in 2nd grade math?
faq.a: It is a long box split into parts. It shows the parts and the whole, so children can see if they need to add or subtract.

faq.q: Why is “Sam has 12 more than Ava” so hard?
faq.a: Children see “more” and add. But if the story gives Sam's number, Ava has 12 fewer, so you subtract. Drawing two bars helps.

faq.q: What does the box mean in an equation like ☐ − 8 = 15?
faq.a: The box stands for the unknown number. Here it is the start, so the answer is 15 + 8 = 23.

items.q: Owen baked 15 cookies. Then he baked 13 more cookies. How many cookies are there now?
items.e: 13 more were added, so add: 15 + 13 = ☐. 15 + 13 = 28. Answer: 28 cookies.

items.q: Ben had 19 toy cars. For his birthday, he got 33 more toy cars. How many toy cars does Ben have now?
items.e: 33 more were added, so add: 19 + 33 = ☐. 19 + 33 = 52. Regroup: 9 + 3 = 12 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 52 toy cars.

items.q: Sofia put 47 beads on a string. Then she added 13 more beads. How many beads are on the string now?
items.e: 13 more were added, so add: 47 + 13 = ☐. 47 + 13 = 60. Regroup: 7 + 3 = 10 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 60 beads.

items.q: Kai had 25 apples in a basket. He picked 45 more apples. How many apples does Kai have now?
items.e: 45 more were added, so add: 25 + 45 = ☐. 25 + 45 = 70. Regroup: 5 + 5 = 10 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 70 apples.

items.q: There were 85 cars in a parking lot. Then 23 cars drove away. How many cars are in the lot now?
items.e: 23 were taken away, so subtract: 85 − 23 = ☐. 85 − 23 = 62. Answer: 62 cars.

items.q: Noah had 77 pennies in a jar. He took 49 pennies out to buy a pencil. How many pennies are in the jar now?
items.e: 49 were taken away, so subtract: 77 − 49 = ☐. 77 − 49 = 28. You cannot take 9 from 7 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 28 pennies.

items.q: There were 33 birds in a tree. 17 birds flew away. How many birds are in the tree now?
items.e: 17 were taken away, so subtract: 33 − 17 = ☐. 33 − 17 = 16. You cannot take 7 from 3 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 16 birds.

items.q: Emma had 24 marbles. She won 17 more marbles in a game. How many marbles does Emma have now?
items.e: 17 more were added, so add: 24 + 17 = ☐. 24 + 17 = 41. Regroup: 4 + 7 = 11 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 41 marbles.

items.q: There were 11 people at the pool. Then 63 more people came. How many people are at the pool now?
items.e: 63 more were added, so add: 11 + 63 = ☐. 11 + 63 = 74. Answer: 74 people.

items.q: A pet store had 75 fish in a tank. The store sold 38 fish. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.e: 38 were taken away, so subtract: 75 − 38 = ☐. 75 − 38 = 37. You cannot take 8 from 5 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 37 fish.

items.q: A farm had 17 chickens. The farmer bought 56 more chickens. How many chickens does the farm have now?
items.e: 56 more were added, so add: 17 + 56 = ☐. 17 + 56 = 73. Regroup: 7 + 6 = 13 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 73 chickens.

items.q: There were 44 children on a bus. At the next stop, 26 children got off. How many children are on the bus now?
items.e: 26 were taken away, so subtract: 44 − 26 = ☐. 44 − 26 = 18. You cannot take 6 from 4 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 18 children.

items.q: There were 36 ducks in a pond. Then 11 more ducks swam over. How many ducks are in the pond now?
items.e: 11 more were added, so add: 36 + 11 = ☐. 36 + 11 = 47. Answer: 47 ducks.

items.q: There were 42 balloons at a party. Then 19 balloons popped. How many balloons are there now?
items.e: 19 were taken away, so subtract: 42 − 19 = ☐. 42 − 19 = 23. You cannot take 9 from 2 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 23 balloons.

items.q: Eli had 49 stickers. He got 19 more stickers from a friend. How many stickers does Eli have now?
items.e: 19 more were added, so add: 49 + 19 = ☐. 49 + 19 = 68. Regroup: 9 + 9 = 18 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 68 stickers.

items.q: Ms. Lee had 51 pencils. She gave 34 pencils to her students. How many pencils does Ms. Lee have now?
items.e: 34 were taken away, so subtract: 51 − 34 = ☐. 51 − 34 = 17. You cannot take 4 from 1 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 17 pencils.

items.q: A library cart had 64 books. Nora took 31 books off the cart. How many books are on the cart now?
items.e: 31 were taken away, so subtract: 64 − 31 = ☐. 64 − 31 = 33. Answer: 33 books.

items.q: Omar had 73 shells. He gave 34 shells to his brother. How many shells does Omar have now?
items.e: 34 were taken away, so subtract: 73 − 34 = ☐. 73 − 34 = 39. You cannot take 4 from 3 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 39 shells.

items.q: Ms. Lee had 32 pencils. She bought 19 more pencils. How many pencils does Ms. Lee have now?
items.e: 19 more were added, so add: 32 + 19 = ☐. 32 + 19 = 51. Regroup: 2 + 9 = 11 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 51 pencils.

items.q: There were 90 people at the pool. Then 34 people went home. How many people are at the pool now?
items.e: 34 were taken away, so subtract: 90 − 34 = ☐. 90 − 34 = 56. You cannot take 4 from 0 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 56 people.

items.q: A small tree has 69 leaves. 31 are green, and the rest are yellow. How many yellow leaves are there?
items.e: You know the whole (69) and one part (31). Find the other part: 31 + ☐ = 69, or 69 − 31 = ☐. 69 − 31 = 38. Answer: 38 leaves.

items.q: Ben has 72 books. 26 are storybooks, and the rest are comic books. How many comic books does he have?
items.e: You know the whole (72) and one part (26). Find the other part: 26 + ☐ = 72, or 72 − 26 = ☐. 72 − 26 = 46. Answer: 46 comic books.

items.q: A toy box has 49 toy cars and 12 toy trucks. How many toys are in the box?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 49 + 12 = ☐. 49 + 12 = 61. Answer: 61 toys.

items.q: Kai has 43 cards. 27 are baseball cards, and the rest are football cards. How many football cards does he have?
items.e: You know the whole (43) and one part (27). Find the other part: 27 + ☐ = 43, or 43 − 27 = ☐. 43 − 27 = 16. Answer: 16 football cards.

items.q: Luis read 55 pages on Monday and 18 pages on Tuesday. How many pages did he read in all?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 55 + 18 = ☐. 55 + 18 = 73. Answer: 73 pages.

items.q: A garden has 75 tulips. 34 are red, and the rest are yellow. How many yellow tulips are there?
items.e: You know the whole (75) and one part (34). Find the other part: 34 + ☐ = 75, or 75 − 34 = ☐. 75 − 34 = 41. Answer: 41 tulips.

items.q: Ruby scored 67 points in two games. She scored 19 points in the first game. How many points did she score in the second game?
items.e: You know the whole (67) and one part (19). Find the other part: 19 + ☐ = 67, or 67 − 19 = ☐. 67 − 19 = 48. Answer: 48 points.

items.q: A pond has 39 ducks and 17 geese. How many birds are on the pond?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 39 + 17 = ☐. 39 + 17 = 56. Answer: 56 birds.

items.q: Leo has 67 red marbles and 16 blue marbles. How many marbles does he have in all?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 67 + 16 = ☐. 67 + 16 = 83. Answer: 83 marbles.

items.q: A farmer has 19 brown eggs and 35 white eggs. How many eggs does the farmer have?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 19 + 35 = ☐. 19 + 35 = 54. Answer: 54 eggs.

items.q: There are 58 children at a school picnic. 25 of them are girls. How many boys are at the picnic?
items.e: You know the whole (58) and one part (25). Find the other part: 25 + ☐ = 58, or 58 − 25 = ☐. 58 − 25 = 33. Answer: 33 boys.

items.q: A class planted 85 seeds. 19 were bean seeds, and the rest were corn seeds. How many corn seeds did the class plant?
items.e: You know the whole (85) and one part (19). Find the other part: 19 + ☐ = 85, or 85 − 19 = ☐. 85 − 19 = 66. Answer: 66 seeds.

items.q: A sticker sheet has 38 gold stars and 56 silver stars. How many stars are on the sheet?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 38 + 56 = ☐. 38 + 56 = 94. Answer: 94 stars.

items.q: A bakery made 27 chocolate cupcakes and 56 vanilla cupcakes. How many cupcakes did it make?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 27 + 56 = ☐. 27 + 56 = 83. Answer: 83 cupcakes.

items.q: An animal shelter has 38 cats and 24 dogs. How many animals are at the shelter?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 38 + 24 = ☐. 38 + 24 = 62. Answer: 62 animals.

items.q: Maya bought 59 apples. 17 were green, and the rest were red. How many red apples did she buy?
items.e: You know the whole (59) and one part (17). Find the other part: 17 + ☐ = 59, or 59 − 17 = ☐. 59 − 17 = 42. Answer: 42 apples.

items.q: Nora has 74 marbles. 68 are red, and the rest are blue. How many blue marbles does she have?
items.e: You know the whole (74) and one part (68). Find the other part: 68 + ☐ = 74, or 74 − 68 = ☐. 74 − 68 = 6. Answer: 6 marbles.

items.q: A garden has 76 red tulips and 18 yellow tulips. How many tulips are in the garden?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 76 + 18 = ☐. 76 + 18 = 94. Answer: 94 tulips.

items.q: Ava has 37 baseball cards and 43 football cards. How many cards does she have?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 37 + 43 = ☐. 37 + 43 = 80. Answer: 80 cards.

items.q: A class planted 67 bean seeds and 29 corn seeds. How many seeds did the class plant?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 67 + 29 = ☐. 67 + 29 = 96. Answer: 96 seeds.

sets.title: Compare: how many more or fewer?

items.q: Owen has 42 baseball cards. He has 15 fewer baseball cards than Ben. How many baseball cards does Ben have?
items.e: Owen has 15 fewer than Ben, so Ben has 15 more. Add: 42 + 15 = 57. The word “fewer” is in the story, but you add. Answer: 57 baseball cards.

items.q: Sofia has 75 toy cars. She has 17 fewer toy cars than Kai. How many toy cars does Kai have?
items.e: Sofia has 17 fewer than Kai, so Kai has 17 more. Add: 75 + 17 = 92. The word “fewer” is in the story, but you add. Answer: 92 toy cars.

items.q: Luis has 40 stamps. Noah has 13 fewer stamps than Luis. How many stamps does Noah have?
items.e: Noah has 13 fewer than Luis, so subtract: 40 − 13 = 27. Answer: 27 stamps.

items.q: Ruby has 15 crayons. Emma has 16 more crayons than Ruby. How many crayons does Emma have?
items.e: Emma has 16 more than Ruby, so add: 15 + 16 = 31. Answer: 31 crayons.

items.q: Leo has 32 beads. He has 16 fewer beads than Jack. How many beads does Jack have?
items.e: Leo has 16 fewer than Jack, so Jack has 16 more. Add: 32 + 16 = 48. The word “fewer” is in the story, but you add. Answer: 48 beads.

items.q: Zoe has 57 books. She has 28 fewer books than Sam. How many books does Sam have?
items.e: Zoe has 28 fewer than Sam, so Sam has 28 more. Add: 57 + 28 = 85. The word “fewer” is in the story, but you add. Answer: 85 books.

items.q: Lily scored 53 points. Grace scored 35 fewer points than Lily. How many points did Grace score?
items.e: Grace scored 35 fewer than Lily, so subtract: 53 − 35 = 18. Answer: 18 points.

items.q: Eli read 32 pages. Maya read 26 pages. How many fewer pages did Maya read than Eli?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one: 32 − 26 = ☐. 32 − 26 = 6. Check: 26 + 6 = 32. Answer: 6 pages.

items.q: Nora has 55 stickers. She has 12 more stickers than Omar. How many stickers does Omar have?
items.e: Nora has 12 more than Omar, so Omar has 12 fewer. Subtract: 55 − 12 = 43. The word “more” is in the story, but you subtract. Answer: 43 stickers.

items.q: Ava has 45 rocks. She has 16 more rocks than Mia. How many rocks does Mia have?
items.e: Ava has 16 more than Mia, so Mia has 16 fewer. Subtract: 45 − 16 = 29. The word “more” is in the story, but you subtract. Answer: 29 rocks.

items.q: Owen jumped rope 65 times. Ben jumped rope 17 more times than Owen. How many times did Ben jump rope?
items.e: Ben jumped 17 more than Owen, so add: 65 + 17 = 82. Answer: 82 times.

items.q: Sofia has 81 marbles. She has 19 more marbles than Kai. How many marbles does Kai have?
items.e: Sofia has 19 more than Kai, so Kai has 19 fewer. Subtract: 81 − 19 = 62. The word “more” is in the story, but you subtract. Answer: 62 marbles.

items.q: Luis has 57 shells. Noah has 41 shells. How many fewer shells does Noah have than Luis?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one: 57 − 41 = ☐. 57 − 41 = 16. Check: 41 + 16 = 57. Answer: 16 shells.

items.q: Ruby picked 72 strawberries. Emma picked 55 strawberries. How many more strawberries did Ruby pick than Emma?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one: 72 − 55 = ☐. 72 − 55 = 17. Check: 55 + 17 = 72. Answer: 17 strawberries. The word “more” does not mean add here.

items.q: Zoe has 62 stickers. Sam has 35 stickers. How many more stickers does Zoe have than Sam?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one: 62 − 35 = ☐. 62 − 35 = 27. Check: 35 + 27 = 62. Answer: 27 stickers. The word “more” does not mean add here.

items.q: Eli has 80 toy cars. Maya has 48 toy cars. How many more toy cars does Eli have than Maya?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one: 80 − 48 = ☐. 80 − 48 = 32. Check: 48 + 32 = 80. Answer: 32 toy cars. The word “more” does not mean add here.

items.q: Nora has 54 rocks. Omar has 16 more rocks than Nora. How many rocks does Omar have?
items.e: Omar has 16 more than Nora, so add: 54 + 16 = 70. Answer: 70 rocks.

items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one: 37 − 19 = ☐. 37 − 19 = 18. Check: 19 + 18 = 37. Answer: 18 beads.

sets.title: Find the missing start or change

items.q: Owen had 63 marbles. He lost some marbles in a game. Now he has 21 marbles. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 63 − ☐ = 21. Think: what number takes 63 down to 21? 63 − 21 = 42. Answer: 42 marbles.

items.q: Ben put some beads on a string. Then he took off 54 beads. Now there are 36 beads on the string. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 54 were taken away, so ☐ − 54 = 36. To solve it, put the 54 back: 36 + 54 = 90. Answer: 90 beads.

items.q: Ms. Lee had 19 pencils. She bought some more pencils. Now she has 34 pencils. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 19 + ☐ = 34. Count up from 19 to 34, or subtract: 34 − 19 = 15. Answer: 15 pencils.

items.q: There were 37 birds in a tree. Some more birds flew to the tree. Now there are 48 birds in the tree. How many birds flew to the tree?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 37 + ☐ = 48. Count up from 37 to 48, or subtract: 48 − 37 = 11. Answer: 11 birds.

items.q: Luis had 47 pennies in a jar. He put some more pennies in the jar. Now there are 66 pennies in the jar. How many pennies did Luis put in?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 47 + ☐ = 66. Count up from 47 to 66, or subtract: 66 − 47 = 19. Answer: 19 pennies.

items.q: Noah baked 31 cookies. His family ate some of the cookies. Now there are 12 cookies. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 31 − ☐ = 12. Think: what number takes 31 down to 12? 31 − 12 = 19. Answer: 19 cookies.

items.q: There were 38 cars in a parking lot. Then some more cars came in. Now there are 79 cars in the lot. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 38 + ☐ = 79. Count up from 38 to 79, or subtract: 79 − 38 = 41. Answer: 41 cars.

items.q: There were some balloons at a party. Then 29 balloons popped. Now there are 25 balloons. How many balloons were there at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 29 were taken away, so ☐ − 29 = 25. To solve it, put the 29 back: 25 + 29 = 54. Answer: 54 balloons.

items.q: Leo had some toy cars. For his birthday, he got 28 more toy cars. Now he has 45 toy cars. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 28 more were added, so ☐ + 28 = 45. To solve it, take the 28 away: 45 − 28 = 17. Answer: 17 toy cars.

items.q: Jack had some apples in a basket. He used 36 apples to make pies. Now he has 23 apples. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 36 were taken away, so ☐ − 36 = 23. To solve it, put the 36 back: 23 + 36 = 59. Answer: 59 apples.

items.q: A farm had 83 chickens. The farmer sold some chickens. Now the farm has 24 chickens. How many chickens did the farmer sell?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 83 − ☐ = 24. Think: what number takes 83 down to 24? 83 − 24 = 59. Answer: 59 chickens.

items.q: There were 53 children on a bus. At the next stop, some children got off. Now there are 26 children on the bus. How many children got off?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 53 − ☐ = 26. Think: what number takes 53 down to 26? 53 − 26 = 27. Answer: 27 children.

items.q: There were some ducks in a pond. Then 31 ducks swam away. Now there are 13 ducks in the pond. How many ducks were in the pond at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 31 were taken away, so ☐ − 31 = 13. To solve it, put the 31 back: 13 + 31 = 44. Answer: 44 ducks.

items.q: There were some people at the pool. Then 47 more people came. Now there are 63 people at the pool. How many people were at the pool at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 47 more were added, so ☐ + 47 = 63. To solve it, take the 47 away: 63 − 47 = 16. Answer: 16 people.

items.q: A pet store had 33 fish in a tank. The owner put in some more fish. Now there are 52 fish in the tank. How many fish did the owner put in?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 33 + ☐ = 52. Count up from 33 to 52, or subtract: 52 − 33 = 19. Answer: 19 fish.

items.q: Maya had some stickers. She got 43 more stickers from a friend. Now she has 68 stickers. How many stickers did Maya have at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 43 more were added, so ☐ + 43 = 68. To solve it, take the 43 away: 68 − 43 = 25. Answer: 25 stickers.

items.q: A library cart had 61 books. Nora took some books off the cart. Now the cart has 12 books. How many books did Nora take off the cart?
items.e: The change is unknown, so it is the ☐: 61 − ☐ = 12. Think: what number takes 61 down to 12? 61 − 12 = 49. Answer: 49 books.

items.q: Omar had some shells. He gave 68 shells to his brother. Now he has 17 shells. How many shells did Omar have at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 68 were taken away, so ☐ − 68 = 17. To solve it, put the 68 back: 17 + 68 = 85. Answer: 85 shells.

items.q: Ava had some apples in a basket. She picked 15 more apples. Now she has 56 apples. How many apples did Ava have at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, so it is the ☐. 15 more were added, so ☐ + 15 = 56. To solve it, take the 15 away: 56 − 15 = 41. Answer: 41 apples.

items.q: Some children were on a bus. At the next stop, 17 more children got on. Now there are 55 children on the bus. Which equation matches the story?

items.q: Owen has 80¢. He buys a pencil for 20¢ and an eraser for 26¢. How much money does he have left?
Sofia had 43 stickers. She got 18 more. Then she gave 22 stickers to her sister. How many stickers does Sofia have now?
items.e: Step 1: Got more: 43 + 18 = 61. Step 2: Gave away: 61 − 22 = 39. Equation: 43 + 18 − 22 = ☐. Answer: 39 stickers.

items.q: A ribbon is 80 cm long. Kai cuts off 16 cm. Then he cuts off 12 cm more. How long is the ribbon now?
items.e: Step 1: First cut: 80 − 16 = 64 cm. Step 2: Second cut: 64 − 12 = 52 cm. Equation: 80 − 16 − 12 = ☐. Answer: 52 cm.

items.q: Noah has 25 stamps. Ruby has 67 stamps. Then Noah gets 8 more stamps. How many more stamps does Ruby have than Noah now?
items.e: Step 1: Noah now: 25 + 8 = 33. Step 2: How many more: 67 − 33 = 34. Equation: 67 − 25 − 8 = ☐. Answer: 34 stamps.

items.q: Leo has 34 shells. Jack has 9 more shells than Leo. How many shells do they have in all?
items.e: Step 1: Jack's shells: 34 + 9 = 43. Step 2: In all: 34 + 43 = 77. Equation: 34 + 34 + 9 = ☐. Answer: 77 shells.

items.q: The Tigers scored 22 points in the first half and 28 points in the second half. The Bears scored 35 points in all. How many more points did the Tigers score than the Bears?
items.e: Step 1: Tigers in all: 22 + 28 = 50. Step 2: How many more: 50 − 35 = 15. Equation: 22 + 28 − 35 = ☐. Answer: 15 points.

items.q: Grandma baked 26 cookies on Saturday and 18 cookies on Sunday. The family ate 13 cookies. How many cookies are left?
items.e: Step 1: Cookies baked: 26 + 18 = 44. Step 2: Left: 44 − 13 = 31. Equation: 26 + 18 − 13 = ☐. Answer: 31 cookies.

items.q: Lily had 61 toy cars. She gave 18 to her cousin and 7 to a friend. How many toy cars does Lily have left?
items.e: Step 1: Gave to the cousin: 61 − 18 = 43. Step 2: Gave to a friend: 43 − 7 = 36. Equation: 61 − 18 − 7 = ☐. Answer: 36 toy cars.

items.q: Ms. Diaz has 28 red pencils and 15 blue pencils. She gives 22 pencils to her students. How many pencils does she have left?
items.e: Step 1: Pencils in all: 28 + 15 = 43. Step 2: Left: 43 − 22 = 21. Equation: 28 + 15 − 22 = ☐. Answer: 21 pencils.

items.q: There were 59 cars in a parking lot. 9 more cars came in. Then 20 cars drove away. How many cars are in the lot now?
items.e: Step 1: Came in: 59 + 9 = 68. Step 2: Drove away: 68 − 20 = 48. Equation: 59 + 9 − 20 = ☐. Answer: 48 cars.

items.q: 33 children were playing outside. 18 children went inside. Then 19 more children came out to play. How many children are outside now?
items.e: Step 1: Went inside: 33 − 18 = 15. Step 2: Came out: 15 + 19 = 34. Equation: 33 − 18 + 19 = ☐. Answer: 34 children.

items.q: A pet store had 22 fish. The owner put in 15 more fish. Then the store sold 18 fish. How many fish are in the store now?
items.e: Step 1: Put in: 22 + 15 = 37. Step 2: Sold: 37 − 18 = 19. Equation: 22 + 15 − 18 = ☐. Answer: 19 fish.

items.q: A bus had 35 people on it. At the first stop, 18 people got off and 16 people got on. How many people are on the bus now?
items.e: Step 1: Got off: 35 − 18 = 17. Step 2: Got on: 17 + 16 = 33. Equation: 35 − 18 + 16 = ☐. Answer: 33 people.

items.q: There were 40 balloons at a party. 7 balloons popped. Then Ava blew up 15 more. How many balloons are there now?
items.e: Step 1: Popped: 40 − 7 = 33. Step 2: Blew up more: 33 + 15 = 48. Equation: 40 − 7 + 15 = ☐. Answer: 48 balloons.

items.q: There were 48 birds in a tree. 15 birds flew away. Then 13 more birds flew away. How many birds are in the tree now?
items.e: Step 1: First group: 48 − 15 = 33. Step 2: Second group: 33 − 13 = 20. Equation: 48 − 15 − 13 = ☐. Answer: 20 birds.

items.q: A red box has 40 beads. A blue box has 8 fewer beads than the red box. How many beads are in both boxes?
items.e: Step 1: Blue box: 40 − 8 = 32. Step 2: Both boxes: 40 + 32 = 72. Equation: 40 + 40 − 8 = ☐. Answer: 72 beads.

items.q: A class wants to read 100 books. The children read 27 books in May and 24 books in June. How many more books do they need to read?
items.e: Step 1: Books read: 27 + 24 = 51. Step 2: Still to read: 100 − 51 = 49. Equation: 100 − 27 − 24 = ☐. Answer: 49 books.

items.q: A school bus has 40 seats. 18 children sit down. Then 8 more children get on and sit down. How many seats are empty now?
items.e: Step 1: Children on the bus: 18 + 8 = 26. Step 2: Empty seats: 40 − 26 = 14. Equation: 40 − 18 − 8 = ☐. Answer: 14 seats.

items.q: Ruby has 37 red beads and 39 blue beads. She uses 41 beads to make a necklace. How many beads are left?
items.e: Step 1: Beads in all: 37 + 39 = 76. Step 2: Left: 76 − 41 = 35. Equation: 37 + 39 − 41 = ☐. Answer: 35 beads.

items.q: Leo read 32 pages. Jack read 14 more pages than Leo. Zoe read 7 fewer pages than Jack. How many pages did Zoe read?
items.e: Step 1: Jack: 32 + 14 = 46 pages. Step 2: Zoe: 46 − 7 = 39 pages. Equation: 32 + 14 − 7 = ☐. Answer: 39 pages.
